endonym.gloss: wide-talk, the same root as the name the speakers use for themselves

description.value: Long low calls made in deep water, audible to a listener four kilometres down a channel and to an instrument considerably further, with a second layer of patterned electrical pulses that carries at conversational range only. The audible layer holds place, movement and weather; the electrical layer holds who is present, which is why a recording of the sound alone is a message with the participants removed. Calls are slow, and a full exchange between two grazers can take most of an hour without either party treating that as a delay. The standing error is to record in the audible band, publish the transcript, and then argue about whether it has syntax.

sampleGloss.value: Uu-waa-nel, uu-uu. long-low-here / who-is-with-me. Free translation: I am on the third vent apron and these four are with me. The four are in the electrical layer and are not in the audio file.

note.value: Recorded during elicitation and kept as the reference sample for this system.

notes.value: The syntax question has been argued since 2271 on the basis of one nineteen-hour recording. Both principal proponents have changed sides, on different occasions, and neither has withdrawn anything published before the change.
